column3: The Hebrew describes Saul at his accession as “a son of a year” and gives two years of reign; BSB has thirty and forty-two.
The Hebrew explicitly names Saul when he chooses the three thousand and sends each remaining man to his tents, plural; BSB uses “he” and “his own home”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the people being called after Saul; BSB says they were summoned to join him.
The Hebrew numbers the chariots as thirty thousand; BSB has three thousand.
The Hebrew repeats “the people” as those hiding; BSB leaves that subject implicit after “the men of Israel”.
The Hebrew says “Hebrews” without a separate “some” or “even”, and calls the trembling group “all the people”.
The Hebrew leaves Saul unnamed in both clauses, whereas BSB repeats his name. The people scatter from him; BSB describes desertion.
The Hebrew explicitly names Saul as speaker; BSB uses “he”.
The Hebrew gives the purpose as blessing Samuel; BSB says greeting him.
The Hebrew explicitly calls the appointed time a time of days and calls the scattering group “the people”; BSB uses “troops”.
The Hebrew retains the image of the LORD’s face and separately narrates self-compulsion and offering; BSB has seeking favor and feeling compelled to offer.
The Hebrew explicitly names Samuel and Saul and has “for now” rather than an explicit “if you had”.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name three times; BSB replaces the middle occurrence with an implicit subject.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls those with Saul and Jonathan “the people”; BSB says “troops”.
The Hebrew uses a singular collective for the raiding force; BSB uses plural “raiders”.
The Hebrew repeats “one division turned” with both divisions; BSB gives the two routes elliptically.
Sword and spear are singular in the Hebrew; BSB uses plurals and makes permission explicit.
The Hebrew says each man sharpened his own tools, naming them individually in the singular; BSB uses collective plural tool names.
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat a weight or sharpening fee in the latter clauses; BSB repeats “a third of a shekel”.
The Hebrew has singular “hand” and repeats the passive finding for Saul and Jonathan; BSB uses plural “hands” and “had weapons”.
Close to the Hebrew.
